A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAOT research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–G support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original GAOT prediction errors, computational benchmarks, scaling experiments, repeated-run results and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds GAOT results in Table E.8 for one DrivAerNet++ test case and an average across 1154 test samples. The imported CarBench baseline results are separately attributed.

M1.justification: The MAGNO encoder/decoder, geometry embeddings, transformer processor, losses and time-stepping procedures are unchanged. The revised benchmark configuration and clarified Poisson input representation do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The datasets, physical domains and PDE coverage are retained. The CarBench comparison reuses DrivAerNet++ with different resolution procedures. Appendix D.1 clarifies the existing Poisson-C-Sines input representation without establishing replacement or expansion of the underlying dataset.

E2.justification: v3's DrivAerNet++ Table 3 compares GAOT with FIGConvNet, TripNet and RegDGCNN. v4 retains this table and adds a broad CarBench comparison against eleven baselines, including PointMAE, PointTransformer, Transolver++, AB-UPT and larger PointNet/Transolver variants. This substantially expands the industrial comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6.4 changes the reported DrivAerNet++ latent grid from [64, 32, 32] to [64, 64, 32], without establishing a rerun. New Section E.9 compares 10k-point baseline training and full-resolution evaluation/interpolation with full-resolution GAOT, reporting MAE, RMSE, relative L2 and R-squared for a single case and GAOT's test-set average.

E4.justification: New Section E.9 extends the full-versus-low-resolution analysis through the CarBench industrial comparison. It supplements the retained DrivAerNet++ neural-field results and NACA0012 comparison with UPT. Existing component ablations, scaling, transfer-learning and resolution-invariance studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The Bluff-Body randomness study still uses six independent seeds and reports 2.39 ± 0.12. It moves from Section E.10/Table E.8 to Section E.11/Table E.9. No new uncertainty estimates, repeated-run practices or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. New Table E.8 adds CarBench comparator scores and GAOT results: RMSE 22.8 and relative L2 0.145 for sample 648, versus 23.9 and 0.157 averaged over 1154 samples. These are additional results under the stated comparison conditions, not improvements over v3's corresponding scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 refines the formal Poisson-C-Sines task from a source-to-solution mapping to a load-vector-to-nodal-solution mapping. It defines load entries through integrals against finite-element basis functions and identifies the mapping as the inverse discrete stiffness operator. The general formulation and architecture derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding summary retain the same central contributions: geometry-aware multiscale operator learning, improved accuracy and computational efficiency, scalability and industrial performance. The added resolution comparison supports these retained claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 expands the argument favoring full-resolution training and acknowledges that AB-UPT's neural-field evaluation, beyond interpolation, needs further investigation. It removes the concluding Limitations and Extensions paragraph, including proposed downstream applications and the statement that universal-approximation results remain future work.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 now explains finite-element load-vector construction and boundary-condition enforcement. The industrial latent-grid specification is revised, and Section E.9 identifies resolutions, interpolation, the selected test case and aggregation size. Code-access information and most implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds CarBench and AB-UPT references and discusses their relevance to industrial resolution comparisons. Removing the extensions paragraph also removes citations concerning DPOT, physics-informed operators, uncertainty quantification, inverse problems and optimization. The main positioning against graph, Fourier and transformer approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The edits are localized: Appendix D.1 is rewritten, Section E.9 and a main-text pointer are added, acknowledgements are expanded, and the concluding extensions paragraph is removed. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table E.8, revises input-panel color scales in Figures G.1–G.3, and redistributes some existing tables and figures across pages. The corresponding ground-truth and prediction panels are unchanged, as are the other matched figure assets.

improvement.justification: The more precise Poisson input definition and added CarBench comparison modestly improve technical transparency and industrial evaluation. The comparison explicitly documents differing training resolutions and acknowledges unresolved neural-field evaluation, although it does not isolate resolution effects from model differences. Removing the extensions paragraph loses some qualification, but the retained scientific evidence and added documentation support a limited net improvement.
